name: Oil & Exploration
scope: Upstream oil & gas - global markets, India's production, policy and pricing, and what they mean for Indian listed producers, service and equipment companies, the gas chain and refiners.

summary.one_line: A war-driven supply shock has lifted crude and Indian upstream profits to records, but Indian output keeps falling, import dependence is at a record 88.7%, and the gains are concentrated in producers while refiners, city gas and LNG importers carry the cost (S1; S2; S3).
key_points: The Strait of Hormuz has been shut or badly impaired since 28 February 2026; the World Bank calls it the largest oil supply shock on record, with an initial loss of about 10 mb/d, and more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output was still shut in during August (S1; S4; S5).

Brent averaged $91/bbl in August 2026 and spiked to $113.48 on 9 September; the EIA now forecasts $91 for 2026 and $74 for 2027, and most banks expect prices to ease in 2027 as Gulf supply returns (S6; S7; S8; S9).
OPEC spare capacity has collapsed to an EIA-estimated 0.43 mb/d for 2026 (3.43 mb/d in 2025), and the UAE left OPEC and OPEC+ on 1 May 2026 (S6; S10).
India produced 27.9 MMT of crude in FY26, down from 32.2 MMT in FY20, and April-July 2026 output was about 4.2% lower again; crude import dependence reached a record 88.7% (S2; S11).

Producers are the clear winners: ONGC's standalone Q1 FY27 profit rose 112% on a $99.45/bbl realisation and Oil India's standalone PAT rose about 3.5x, but HPCL's loss cut ONGC's consolidated profit by 43% (S3; S12; S13).

APM gas is capped at $7.00/MMBtu while the formula price is $9.00 for September 2026, so domestic gas gains far less than crude; new-well gas (priced higher, no cap) earned ONGC $13.31/MMBtu (S3; S14).

Policy is turning pro-exploration: Samudra Manthan (₹84,084 cr to FY31, 60 deepwater wells with up to 50% government cost support), OALP-X and XI (46 blocks), and a new single petroleum lease regime (S15; S16; S17; S18).

State refiners lost money in Q1 FY27 with pump prices frozen (HPCL ₹12,264 cr, IOC ₹2,661 cr standalone), city gas margins were squeezed, and Petronet's Dahej terminal ran at 66% (S19; S20; S21; S22).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Crude producers with Brent-linked realisations: ONGC, Oil India, Vedanta Oil & Gas and small E&Ps such as Antelopus Selan and HOEC (S3; S12; S23; S24; S25).
Oil India also gains from Numaligarh refinery margins ($35.95/bbl GRM) and 11% crude volume growth (S12).
Global line-pipe makers riding Gulf and US gas pipeline capex: Welspun Corp's order book is about $4.4 bn after a $1.8 bn US order (S26).
Seismic, drilling and pipe suppliers if Samudra Manthan and OALP awards turn into orders (Asian Energy, Maharashtra Seamless, Deep Industries) (S15; S27; S28).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Oil marketing companies while retail fuel prices stay frozen: BPCL had ₹15,803 cr of cumulative LPG under-recovery at 30 June 2026 (S19).
City gas distributors with Brent-linked gas costs (IGL profit −48%, MGL margin down to ₹7.9/scm) (S21; S29).
LNG importers and regas terminals when Qatar cargoes are disrupted (S30; S31).
Shallow-water rig contractors face ONGC's pricing power: Jindal Drilling bid $62,000/day and won about $47,600 (S32).
A ceasefire that reopens Hormuz: Goldman's downside case has Brent in the $60s, and the IEA sees a 2027 surplus (S8; S33).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Hormuz shipping traffic and the 4 October 2026 OPEC+ meeting (S4; S34).
Any windfall tax or levy on domestic crude - its 2026 status is not confirmed by a primary source (S35).
PPAC's monthly production data and the October 2026 HPHT gas price ceiling notification (S2; S11).
ONGC's first Mahanadi deepwater well result (expected by end-September 2026) and OALP-X/XI deepwater bids on 15 November 2026 (S17; S36).

sections.title: Global picture: the largest supply shock on record

blocks.text: A US-Israel war with Iran broke out in late February 2026. Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz to normal commercial traffic on 28 February, and daily transits fell from more than 100 vessels to about five (S4). A ceasefire in early April and a mid-June memorandum reopened the strait from around 17 June, but the deal broke down in early July after attacks on commercial ships, and routine traffic stopped again (S4; S37).

The World Bank called it the largest oil supply shock on record, with an initial loss of about 10 mb/d (S1). In August 2026 the IEA still counted more than 10 mb/d of Gulf production shut in, with Gulf exports at about 13 mb/d, nearly half the pre-war level (S5). The EIA puts Hormuz-related crude shut-ins at 6.7 mb/d in August, up from 5.0 mb/d in July (S6).

items: The UAE left OPEC and OPEC+ with effect from 1 May 2026. It pumped 3.4 mb/d in 2025 with 4.2 mb/d of capacity; without it, OPEC+ falls from about 46% to about 42% of world crude output (S10).
The US renewed its blockade of Iranian oil exports and OFAC added sanctions; attacks affecting the Bab el-Mandeb route cut Saudi exports from Yanbu by about half in August versus July (S6).
Saudi crude output fell to 6.24 mb/d in August 2026, its lowest since 1990, according to OPEC secondary sources as compiled by Commodity Context (S38).
Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan in March damaged two LNG trains; QatarEnergy declared force majeure and about 12.8 Mtpa of capacity may be out for 3-5 years (media report) (S39).
More than 30 Middle East energy facilities have been damaged, with repairs running into tens of billions of dollars (IEA) (S40).

blocks.text: The situation changes week to week: Dated Brent was $113.48 on 9 September, and Brent settled near $104 on 11 September after Iran said it would meet Gulf states in Oman to discuss the strait (S7; S41). Figures in this edition are as of 11-14 September 2026.

Brent averaged $69.04/bbl in 2025 (S6). It rose about 65% ($46/bbl) by end-March 2026, its biggest monthly rise ever (S42), and Dated Brent averaged $120.36 in April, trading in an almost $50 range (S43). Quarterly averages were $81.11 in Q1 2026 and $102.93 in Q2 (S6). After easing to about $84 in July, Brent averaged $91 in August (S6; S7).

blocks.text: The IEA's September report expects world oil demand to fall by 2.5 mb/d in 2026 to 102.45 mb/d, then rebound by 2.6 mb/d in 2027; it does not see demand returning to the pre-war level of about 106 mb/d until late 2027 (S45). OPEC still sees growth - 380 kb/d in 2026, after its fifth straight downward revision - and about 2.4 mb/d in 2027 (S46; S47). Before the war, the IEA had forecast 930 kb/d of growth for 2026 (S48).

On supply, the IEA expects 100.7 mb/d in 2026, down 5.7 mb/d, followed by an 8 mb/d rebound in 2027 (S45). OPEC+ crude output is expected to fall 5 mb/d to 34.5 mb/d in 2026 (S45). Observed global inventories have drawn 507 mb since February, including 95 mb in August (S7).

blocks.title: World liquid fuels: production vs consumption

blocks.text: The same data that shows a deficit today shows a glut later: the EIA expects a 1.97 mb/d stock draw in 2026 and a 4.90 mb/d build in 2027 (S6), and the IEA's June report implied a surplus of about 5 mb/d in 2027 (S33). That is why most 2027 price forecasts are well below today's price.

sections.title: India: falling output, record import dependence

blocks.text: India produced 27.9 MMT of crude and condensate in FY26, down from 28.7 MMT in FY25 and 32.2 MMT in FY20 (S2). The Petroleum Minister's reply to the Lok Sabha gives 27.96 MMT, a 2.57% fall (S53). The decline has continued: April-July 2026 output was 9.14 MMT against 9.54 MMT a year earlier, about 4.2% lower (S11).

blocks.title: India crude oil + condensate production
blocks.source: Source: PPAC, India's Oil & Gas Ready Reckoner FY26 (S2)

items: Western Offshore supplied about 43% of FY26 crude, Gujarat onshore 19%, Assam 16%, Rajasthan 11% and Eastern Offshore 10% (S2).
Rajasthan (mainly Vedanta-Cairn's Barmer fields) fell from 6,653 TMT in FY20 to 2,946 TMT in FY26, while Eastern Offshore rose from 557 TMT to 2,725 TMT on KG-D6 and ONGC's KG-DWN-98/2 (S2).
ONGC's Q1 FY27 standalone crude output fell 5.5% and gas about 2%, which it blamed on reservoir issues, rough seas delaying pipeline work and well shutdowns during commissioning (S3).

blocks.caption: FY26 crude production by regime (MMT)
rows: ONGC reports 20.6 MMT including its JV share (S2; S54)
Includes Vedanta-Cairn Rajasthan and RIL-bp KG-D6 (S2)

blocks.text: The trends differ: ONGC's nomination output fell every year from 19.2 MMT (FY20) to 16.8 MMT (FY26), private and JV output fell from 8.2 to 5.7 MMT, while Oil India grew from 3.1 to 3.4 MMT (S2). In April-July 2026 Oil India's nomination output rose to 1.28 MMT from 1.13 MMT, while ONGC and PSC blocks both fell (S11).

Gross gas production peaked at 36,438 MMSCM in FY24 and fell to 34,776 MMSCM (about 34.8 BCM) in FY26 (S2). By operator, ONGC produced 18,481 MMSCM, Oil India 3,099 MMSCM and PSC/JV fields 13,195 MMSCM - triple the PSC/JV level of FY21, driven by KG-D6 (S2). April-July 2026 output was about 4.3% lower year on year (S56).

items: Reliance-bp KG-D6 averaged 24.8 MMSCMD in Q1 FY27 at a realised $8.89/MMBtu, down from $9.97 a year earlier (S57).
APM gas from ONGC and Oil India legacy fields is about 60% of domestic production, at about 92 MMSCMD (S58).
LNG imports were 34,216 MMSCM in FY26, and LNG met 49.2% of gas consumption (S2).

blocks.text: India imported 245.4 MMT of crude worth $123.1 bn in FY26, against $137.2 bn in FY25 and $133.4 bn in FY24 (S2). The net bill for crude and products after product exports was $102.9 bn (S2). Refineries processed 272.1 MMT of crude, 90.6% of it imported (S2), and product consumption rose to 243.2 MMT (S2). As a rule of thumb, every $1/bbl rise in crude adds about $2 bn to the annual import bill (S59).

blocks.text: ONGC's standalone profit rose 112% to ₹17,034 cr on higher realisations (S3), and Oil India's standalone PAT rose from ₹813 cr to ₹2,870 cr (S12). At the other end, IOC posted a standalone loss of ₹2,661 cr (S20), BPCL a consolidated loss of ₹1,873 cr (S19) and HPCL a consolidated loss of ₹12,264 cr (S19). Because ONGC owns about 54% of HPCL, ONGC's consolidated profit fell 43% to ₹6,554 cr (S13; S67).

Gas businesses were squeezed too: IGL's net profit fell 48% (S21), and Petronet's Dahej terminal ran at 66% utilisation against 92% a year earlier (S22). Line-pipe exporters did well - Welspun Corp's EBITDA rose 35% (S69).

At the start of the war Emkay Global said the 'best protection may come from upstream stocks such as ONGC and Oil India', while warning that windfall taxes could offset some of the gains (S59). Q1 FY27 results bore out the first half of that call; the tax risk remains open.

Since April 2023, gas from ONGC and Oil India nomination fields is priced at 10% of the monthly Indian crude basket, with a $4/MMBtu floor and a ceiling; gas from new wells or well interventions gets a 20% premium (S70). The ceiling was $6.50 for FY24 and FY25, $6.75 from April 2025 and $7.00 from April 2026 (S58). With the crude basket near $100 the formula gives far more than the ceiling: $10.76 in April, $11.59 in May and $9.00 for September 2026 (S2; S14).

What this means: APM gas is about 60% of domestic output (S58) and is capped at $7, so producers gain little from crude above about $70 (S58). New-well gas carries no cap: ONGC realised $13.31/MMBtu on it in Q1 FY27, earning ₹1,897 cr more than APM pricing would have (S3).

The windfall tax (Special Additional Excise Duty) on domestic crude, introduced in July 2022, was abolished with effect from 2 December 2024 (S35). In May 2026 the government cut royalty on nomination blocks, but in early June it reset onshore nomination and pre-NELP rates; Business Standard estimates the reversal cuts Oil India's EPS by 5-6% and ONGC's by about 1.4% (S71).

Unconfirmed: some explainer sites say a windfall tax on domestic crude returned in March 2026, but we found no primary notification. ONGC's Q1 FY27 realisation of $99.45/bbl suggests no large crude levy (S3). Kotak expects any windfall tax to be short-lived (S60). Check CBIC notifications before relying on either view.

items: The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act separates petroleum from mining, creates a single 'petroleum lease', raises penalties and adds dispute resolution; Lok Sabha passed it on 12 March 2025 (S72).
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025 allow a lease of up to 30 years (extendable to field life), add a stabilisation clause and set a 180-day limit for deciding lease applications (S18).

Nearly 1 million sq km of former 'No-Go' offshore area was opened in 2022; companies have reported 172 discoveries since 2015, 62 of them offshore (S73). The target is 1 million sq km under exploration by 2030 (S74).
OALP rounds I-IX awarded 172 blocks over 3,78,652 sq km (S75). In Round IX (April 2025), ONGC won 15 blocks, Oil India 9 (six alone) and Vedanta 7 (S76).

Round X offers 25 blocks, including 12 ultra-deepwater and 4 Andaman blocks - the largest OALP round (sources give its area as 191,986 or 182,589 sq km) (S16). Round XI offers 21 blocks over 80,234 sq km (S17).
Onshore and shallow-water bids for Rounds X and XI closed on 19 June 2026; the deepwater deadline has been pushed to 15 November 2026, reportedly pending Samudra Manthan rules (S17).
Small-field auctions: in DSF Round IV, Antelopus Selan won two onshore blocks and Oilmax (merging into Asian Energy Services) won an offshore Gujarat-Kutch block (S77; S78).

subsections.title: Samudra Manthan: the National Offshore Exploration Scheme

blocks.text: The Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan on 31 July 2026 with an outlay of ₹84,084 cr to FY2030-31 (S15; S79). Subject to exploration success, it aims to raise domestic oil and gas output from about 62 MMTOE to 80 MMTOE a year and grow the resource base from 1.6 to 2.2 billion TOE (S15).

blocks.caption: Scheme components
rows: Acquisition and processing of modern offshore seismic (S15)
60 wells; government pays up to 50% of eligible cost or ₹675 cr per well, whichever is lower (S15)
Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zones
Local manufacturing of critical equipment and services (S15)

blocks.text: Who could benefit first: seismic contractors (the largest component after drilling), deepwater drillers and vessel owners, and pipe and equipment makers. ONGC says it 'will play a major role' and its own exploration spending will fall (S36). Volumes from any discoveries are unlikely before the 2030s (S60).
Spare capacity is the market's shock absorber. The IEA says OPEC+ spare capacity hit a historic low of 170 kb/d in April 2026, with Gulf barrels locked behind the strait (S43).

Output outside the Gulf keeps growing. The IEA expects the US, Canada, Brazil, Guyana and Argentina to add 1.4 mb/d in 2026 and 1 mb/d in 2027 (S45). In 2025 world supply rose 3 mb/d, 1.8 mb/d of it from outside OPEC+, and stocks built by 470 mb (S48).

items: OPEC+ unwound its 2.2 mb/d of voluntary cuts from April 2025, paused increases for January-March 2026, and completed unwinding the 1.65 mb/d April-2023 cuts with a final 188 kb/d rise for September 2026 (S80; S81; S82).
On 6 September 2026 seven OPEC+ countries kept October output unchanged; the next meeting is on 4 October 2026 (S34).

Sanctions: OFAC sanctioned Rosneft and Lukoil (about 55% of Russian output) from November 2025, and Venezuelan exports fell from 880 kb/d to about 300 kb/d in January 2026 under the US blockade (S48; S83).

blocks.text: Demand held up despite prices: refineries processed 23.77 MMT in July 2026, up 2.0% year on year (OPIS report) (S84).

subsections.title: What producers actually realised in Q1 FY27

blocks.text: Dated Brent averaged $104.5/bbl in April-June 2026, $36.7 higher than a year earlier (S57), and the Indian crude basket averaged $100.74 (S20).
KG-D6 gas is priced under the deepwater ceiling, which is set from lagged fuel prices, so its realisation fell even as Brent rose (S2; S57).

items: ONGC: moving Kotak's crude assumption from $65 to $85/bbl for FY27 lifted its standalone EBITDA estimate by 40%, roughly 2% per $1/bbl (our arithmetic, not Kotak's statement) (S60).

ONGC in practice: nomination crude realisation rose $33/bbl and standalone PAT more than doubled, even with crude volumes down about 5% (S36). Management describes its pricing as 'Brent plus 1%' and expects the Q1 premium to normalise (S60).
Oil India in practice: realisation +$26.2/bbl and volume +11% took standalone PAT from ₹813 cr to ₹2,870 cr (S12).
APM gas does not move above about $70 crude because of the $7 ceiling; new-well gas is priced at 12% of oil with no cap (S58; S60).
A brokerage cited by Business Standard says ONGC and Oil India share prices imply about $60/bbl net realisation, while actual realisations could be 35-50% higher (S85).
Refiners: Nomura estimates each ₹1/litre change in excise duty moves FY26F EBITDA by 13.5% for HPCL, 12.4% for BPCL and 10.9% for IOC (S67).

blocks.text: We found no current note from a named broker with an explicit 'each $1/bbl changes EPS by X%' table for ONGC or Oil India. A widely repeated rule of thumb of ₹300-400 cr of revenue per $1/bbl has no named source and is low confidence (S86).

blocks.caption: Cost structure
rows: EBITDA margin about 70% in Q1 FY27

blocks.text: Hormuz carried almost 20% of global LNG supply. The IEA expects Qatar and UAE LNG supply to fall about 45% (54 bcm) in 2026, offset by close to 50 bcm from new projects elsewhere (S31), and puts cumulative Middle East LNG losses at 140 bcm over 2026-2030 (S31). In Q2 2026, TTF averaged close to $16/MMBtu and Asian spot LNG $17.5, the highest Q2 levels since 2022, while Henry Hub averaged $2.95 (S31). TTF was €79.52/MWh on 11 September with EU storage about 67% full (S87).

blocks.title: Gas price benchmarks, World Bank (2026-27 forecast)
blocks.source: Source: World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook, April 2026 (S44)

items: US LNG exports are forecast to rise from 15 Bcf/d in 2025 to 19 Bcf/d in 2027, with Henry Hub at $3.28 in 2027 (S6).
2025 was a record year for LNG final investment decisions (more than 100 bcm, about 90% in the US), and 230 bcm of capacity outside the Gulf is under construction (S40).
For India, cheaper US-linked LNG against oil-linked contracts helps GAIL's portfolio, while high spot prices cut demand from price-sensitive buyers (S22; S64).

blocks.text: The IEA estimates global upstream oil and gas investment at $546 bn in 2026, similar to 2025: gas up 8%, oil slightly down (S40). Oil supply investment falls for a third year to under $500 bn, while gas supply investment reaches a 10-year high of $330 bn (S40). US shale spending falls 7% to $72 bn, while Central and South America rise about 10% to $68 bn (S40).

items: OPEC says $17.7 tn of oil investment is needed in 2026-2050, over $700 bn a year, and sees demand reaching 124 mb/d by 2050 (S88).
The IEA's Stated Policies Scenario has oil demand levelling off near 102 mb/d around 2030; its Current Policies Scenario has no peak before 2050 (S89).
Restoring Venezuela to about 3 mb/d would need several hundred billion dollars over a decade (IEA) (S40).

items: KG-DWN-98/2 (ONGC): oil began in January 2024 but reached only 28,000 bpd by November 2025, against a planned 45,000 bpd (S92). The gas target is now 3 MMSCMD by Q4 FY27 and a 6-7 MMSCMD peak by Q4 FY28, against a design capacity of 10 MMSCMD (S36; S93).

Mumbai High: bp became technical services provider in February 2025, raising oil output by 3,500-4,000 bpd (S94), and the role was extended to 43 Western Offshore blocks on 25 June 2026 (S95). Redevelopment Phase-I is expected to add 2.699 MMT of oil and 2.806 BCM of gas by 2040 (S54).

ONGC's new gas projects should add about 1 BCM a year, including Daman Upside at 2 MMSCMD by December (S13). In FY26 ONGC made three offshore discoveries and replaced 1.17x its production with new reserves (S54).

ONGC spudded India's first deepwater exploration well in the Mahanadi basin in July 2026 (S96), with results expected by end-September (S36). It also drilled the AND-P-1 stratigraphic well in the Andaman deepwater (S97).

Oil India has two Andaman gas finds from three wells (Vijayapuram-2 in September 2025, Vijayapuram-3 in June 2026) (S98). A fourth well is planned for December 2026 and a field assessment for March 2027 (S12).
Oil India targets 4 MTPA of crude in FY27 ('Mission 4+'), up from 3.45 MT in FY26 (S99; S100). Its Numaligarh refinery expansion from 3 to 9 MMTPA is due to finish by 31 March 2027 (S12).
Vedanta Oil & Gas notified a gas discovery at the Kaam BCP-1ST well in Rajasthan, but gross output fell 17% to 77.7 kboepd in Q1 FY27 (S101; S102).
Reliance has drilled 31 of 40 wells in its CBM campaign; CBM output is 1.0 MMSCMD (S57).

subsections.title: Demand for rigs, vessels and services

items: ONGC floated a tender to hire drillships and semi-submersibles for up to five years, with spend estimated at $18-20 bn (S103). It separately cancelled a four-rig tender when bids came in well above expected day rates (S104).
Pricing stays tight even at $100 oil: Jindal Drilling won a three-year ONGC contract at ₹45.83 lakh a day (about $47,900), after bidding $62,000 (S32; S105).
Offshore rates are recovering globally: jack-up utilisation is back to about 70%, and the rig orderbook is only 2.4% of the fleet; Greatship reprices three rigs and four vessels in H2 FY27 (S61).
Well services: Deep Industries' order book is ₹3,047 cr, and its 15-year, ₹1,402 cr ONGC production-enhancement contract should restart around October 2026 (S106).
Seismic: ONGC acquired 4,631 sq km of 3D seismic in FY26 (S54); Oil India empanelled South West Pinnacle for 2D/3D seismic acquisition (S107).
Offshore construction and pipe: L&T won two ultra-mega (above ₹15,000 cr) offshore orders in the Gulf in August 2026 (S63; S108), and Welspun Corp won a record $1.8 bn US gas pipeline order (S26).

Oil India offers more upside; about 25% EPS CAGR FY26-29E; target ₹600 (S85)

[ICRA]AA+ (Stable); low cost, but Rajasthan concentration and PSC expiry in 2030 (S23)
Volumes may fall 8-10% in the LNG disruption; margins largely protected (S66)
Upstream is the best protection; Hormuz could push crude above $90-110 (S59)

blocks.text: Bank forecasts are in the Global picture section. The spread is wide: for late 2026, Citi expects $70 and Morgan Stanley $100 (S9; S50). For 2027, forecasts range from JPMorgan's $64 to HSBC's $85 (S8; S51). Most assume Gulf supply recovers during 2027.

Some broker details come from news summaries because the original notes are paywalled. Business Standard's 19 August piece did not name the firm, and JPMorgan's 2027 view is reported as both $64 and $80 (S52; S85).

items: Peace breaks out: if Hormuz reopens fully, Goldman's downside case puts Brent in the $60s; the EIA already expects $67 in 2H27, and JPMorgan warns oversupply may force OPEC+ cuts (S6; S8; S51).
Windfall tax or new levies: abolished in December 2024, but its 2026 status is unconfirmed and royalty rates have already flip-flopped (S35; S71).
Subsidiary losses: HPCL's under-recoveries halved ONGC's consolidated profit in Q1 FY27 (S13).
Production decline and project delays: national output keeps falling (S11), KG-DWN-98/2 guidance has been cut repeatedly (S93), and Vedanta Oil & Gas's output fell 17% (S102).
Contract expiry: Vedanta's Rajasthan PSC runs to May 2030, and its Cambay extension is in court (S23; S102).

subsections.title: Risks for the rest of the chain

items: Oil marketing companies: losses continue as long as retail prices stay frozen; BPCL alone had ₹15,803 cr of cumulative LPG under-recovery (S19).
Gas supply: Qatar force majeure and LNG shortfalls hit Petronet, GAIL marketing and city gas volumes (S30; S66; S122).
Demand destruction: the IEA expects world oil demand to fall 2.5 mb/d in 2026 (S45).
Service pricing: ONGC's near-monopsony keeps day rates low even when oil is high (S32).
Execution in the Gulf: the conflict disrupted Jindal Saw's exports and adds risk to Gulf pipeline and offshore contracts (S63; S120).

companies.name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd
companies.role: India's largest E&P company, with nominated (APM) and new-well gas, offshore fields such as Mumbai High and KG-DWN-98/2, and onshore fields (S3; S130)
companies.impact: Biggest direct beneficiary of Brent-linked crude (standalone PAT +112% in Q1 FY27) and of uncapped new-well gas; HPCL losses, any windfall tax and KG-98/2 delays are the offsets (S3; S13; S60).

companies.name: Oil India Ltd
companies.role: Second-largest state E&P company, with onshore assets in Assam and Rajasthan plus offshore frontier blocks in Andaman (S12; S131)
companies.impact: Higher beta than ONGC: crude volume +11% plus a $26/bbl higher realisation took standalone PAT about 3.5x; NRL refining and Andaman gas add optionality (S12; S85).

companies.name: Vedanta Oil and Gas Ltd
companies.role: Pure-play upstream company demerged from Vedanta Ltd (demerger effective 1 May 2026; listed 15 June 2026) (S23; S110)
companies.impact: Crude-linked revenue at low cost ($15-16/boe), but output fell 17% in Q1 FY27 and the Rajasthan PSC expires in 2030 (S23; S102).

companies.name: Reliance Industries Ltd
companies.role: Operates the deepwater KG-D6 gas and condensate fields with BP, plus Shahdol coal-bed methane (CBM) (S57)
companies.impact: E&P is small for the group; KG-D6 gas is priced under the deepwater ceiling, so realisations fell even with Brent above $100 (S57).

companies.name: Antelopus Selan Energy Ltd
companies.role: Small private E&P company with onshore Cambay fields (Bakrol, Karjisan, Lohar) and, after merging with Antelopus in 2025, undeveloped KG and Assam discoveries (S24; S77)
companies.impact: Near-pure price play with high operating leverage; two DSF-IV blocks lengthen the growth runway (S24; S77).

companies.name: Hindustan Oil Exploration Co Ltd
companies.role: Small private E&P company: B-80 offshore oil and gas (Mumbai), Dirok gas and condensate (Assam), Kharsang (Arunachal), PY-1 gas (Cauvery) (S112; S113)
companies.impact: Benefits from market-priced gas and higher Brent, but offtake disputes and pipeline limits have mattered more than prices (S25).

companies.name: Jindal Drilling & Industries Ltd
companies.role: Offshore jack-up drilling contractor (owned and managed rigs) working almost entirely for ONGC in shallow water (S32; S105)
companies.impact: Gains from ONGC's offshore drilling push, but ONGC squeezes day rates and three rigs come up for re-tender in FY27 (S32).

companies.name: Deep Industries Ltd
companies.role: Onshore oilfield services: gas compression, drilling and workover rigs, gas dehydration, and production-enhancement contracts (PEC) (S106; S132)
companies.impact: Fixed-rate contracts give low direct price exposure; benefits from ONGC's push to lift output from mature fields (S106).

companies.name: Dolphin Offshore Enterprises (India) Ltd
companies.role: Offshore marine services: underwater diving and engineering, vessel operations, rig and ship repair, marine logistics (S133)
companies.impact: Would benefit from more Western Offshore and Samudra Manthan activity; no 2026 contract details were found (S133).

companies.name: Asian Energy Services Ltd
companies.role: Seismic data acquisition, oilfield O&M and EPC for oil & gas and mining (S28; S78)
companies.impact: Seismic and O&M demand should rise with OALP, DSF and Samudra Manthan surveys; the Oilmax merger adds a producing-block interest (S78).

companies.name: Aban Offshore Ltd
companies.role: Offshore drilling contractor (jack-ups, drillship) (S134; S135)
companies.impact: In insolvency: outcomes for shareholders depend on the process, not on crude (S134).

companies.name: South West Pinnacle Exploration Ltd
companies.role: Drilling and exploration services for minerals, coal-bed methane (CBM) and oil & gas, including seismic (S107)
companies.impact: Moderate hydrocarbon exposure through RIL CBM drilling and Oil India seismic; mining is the main driver (S107).

companies.name: SEAMEC Ltd
companies.role: Owns and charters multi-support and diving support vessels (MSV/DSV) and provides subsea services, largely for ONGC offshore projects (S115; S136)
companies.impact: Levered to ONGC's offshore maintenance and project spend; crude matters indirectly (S115).

companies.name: The Great Eastern Shipping Co Ltd
companies.role: Shipping company with an offshore subsidiary owning 4 jack-up rigs and 19 offshore supply vessels, chartered to ONGC and international operators (S61; S117)
companies.impact: Offshore rigs and vessels reprice through FY27-28 as jack-up utilisation recovers; tankers gain from the supply dislocation (S61).

companies.name: Maharashtra Seamless Ltd
companies.role: Makes seamless and ERW pipes, including oil country tubular goods (OCTG) such as casing, tubing and drill pipe for ONGC and Oil India (S27; S137)
companies.impact: A direct play on the ONGC and Oil India well count; orders follow higher crude with a 2-4 quarter lag (S27).

companies.name: Jindal Saw Ltd
companies.role: Makes large-diameter SAW line pipe, ductile iron pipe and seamless pipe (for the oil & gas and water sectors) (S120)
companies.impact: Regaining certified oil & gas orders after its API licence suspension matters more than crude; Hormuz hurt its exports (S120).

companies.name: Welspun Corp Ltd
companies.role: Global large-diameter line-pipe maker (plants in India, US, Saudi Arabia) supplying oil & gas transmission and water projects (S26; S69)
companies.impact: Levered to US and Saudi gas pipeline capex more than Indian upstream; record $4.4 bn order book (S26; S62).

companies.name: MAN Industries (India) Ltd
companies.role: Makes large-diameter LSAW, HSAW and ERW line pipe for oil & gas, water and city gas; expanding into Saudi Arabia (S118; S119)
companies.impact: Gulf and Indian pipeline capex; the Saudi NPC acquisition brings Aramco approval (S119).

companies.name: Oil Country Tubular Ltd
companies.role: Small maker of drill pipe and other tubular goods (25,000 tpa); ONGC and OIL are its main customers (S138)
companies.impact: Depends on ONGC and Oil India drill-pipe tenders; small and loss-making, with only aggregator data found (low confidence) (S138).

companies.name: Engineers India Ltd
companies.role: Government-owned engineering consultant and turnkey EPC contractor for refineries, petrochemicals, pipelines, and onshore/offshore oil and gas facilities, in India and the Middle East (S121)
companies.impact: Mainly a refinery and petrochemical capex play; OMC balance-sheet stress could slow orders (S121).

companies.name: Larsen & Toubro Ltd
companies.role: L&T Energy Hydrocarbon (LTEH) performs engineering, procurement, construction, installation and commissioning (EPCIC) of offshore platforms, pipelines and onshore oil & gas facilities for ADNOC, Aramco, QatarEnergy and ONGC (S63; S139)
companies.impact: Gulf NOC offshore capex is driving ultra-mega hydrocarbon orders; a small part of group earnings (S63).

companies.name: GAIL (India) Ltd
companies.role: Largest gas transmission and marketing company (pipelines, LNG portfolio), plus petrochemicals and LPG/liquid hydrocarbons (S64; S122)
companies.impact: Mixed: regulated transmission and LPG gain, gas marketing loses volume when LNG is scarce (S64; S122).

companies.name: Petronet LNG Ltd
companies.role: India's largest LNG import and regasification operator (Dahej, Kochi), with long-term Qatar LNG contracts (S22; S30)
companies.impact: Throughput falls when Qatar cargoes are disrupted and spot LNG is costly; tariffs are mostly fixed (S22; S30).

companies.name: Gujarat Energy (formerly Gujarat Gas)
companies.role: City gas distributor (large industrial PNG base in Gujarat) (S123)
companies.impact: Industrial PNG volumes depend on spot LNG prices against propane; less exposed to APM cuts (S124).

companies.name: Indraprastha Gas Ltd
companies.role: City gas distributor for Delhi NCR (CNG and PNG); depends on declining APM gas allocations plus new-well and LNG gas (S21; S65)
companies.impact: Loses when crude rises: Brent-linked gas costs go up faster than CNG prices (S21; S65).

companies.name: Mahanagar Gas Ltd
companies.role: City gas distributor for Mumbai and surrounding areas (CNG and domestic PNG heavy) (S29; S140)
companies.impact: Same squeeze as IGL; CRISIL expects pass-through to protect margins over time (S66).

companies.name: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd
companies.role: Largest refiner and fuel retailer; buys crude, so profits fall when crude rises and retail prices are frozen (S20; S68)
companies.impact: Hurt by frozen pump prices and LPG losses, partly offset by strong refining margins (S67; S68).

companies.name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd
companies.role: State refiner and fuel marketer with a high marketing-to-refining ratio (S19)
companies.impact: Hurt by high crude with frozen retail prices; the highest GRM of the three OMCs cushions it (S67; S68).

companies.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd
companies.role: State refiner and fuel marketer with the highest marketing-to-refining ratio; ONGC owns about 54% (S13; S19)
companies.impact: The most exposed OMC to crude spikes, and its losses flow into ONGC's consolidated profit (S13; S67).

method: Researched by Claude (Anthropic) with live web search and page reads between 12 and 14 September 2026, in three passes: global markets, India, and listed companies. Every figure cites the page it came from. Official statistics and agencies (EIA, IEA, World Bank, OPEC, PPAC, PIB, Parliament replies) were preferred, followed by company filings and rating rationales, broker views and credible news. The most consequential 2026 claims were checked a second time against separate sources: the Hormuz closure, the UAE's exit from OPEC, EIA price forecasts, ONGC's Q1 FY27 results, the Vedanta Oil & Gas listing and the Samudra Manthan outlay. Some company details come from AI-written earnings-call summaries (GuruFocus, Multibagg) and are marked by publisher; check them against exchange filings. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini were not used. Known gaps: no named broker table of EPS change per $1/bbl, 2026 windfall-tax status, OALP-X/XI results, the IEA and OPEC September reports (paywalled; taken from press coverage), and an official Indian rig count. Company numbers in the table refresh daily from screener.in; this research is updated monthly.
